issues.description: Sensitive payment card data (cardNumber, expiryDate, cvv) exposed in interface and stored in memory without encryption. Violates PCI DSS compliance and exposes sensitive data to memory dumps, logging, and accidental exposure.
issues.suggestion: Never handle full card details in application code. Use PCI-compliant payment gateway (Stripe, Square) with tokenization. Store only token, not card data. Interface should contain only: { paymentToken: string; amount: number; }

issues.description: Card validation logic uses weak validation rules. Only validates card number length (16 digits) without LUHN algorithm. Card validation should never happen locally.
issues.suggestion: Remove all local card validation. Let payment processor validate the card. Use PCI-compliant processor tokens instead of raw card data.

issues.description: Expiry date parsing uses weak logic creating date at start of month instead of end. Could allow use of expired cards. Proper validation should be done by payment processor.
issues.suggestion: Fix expiry validation to use last day of month: const expiryDate = new Date(2000 + parseInt(year), parseInt(month), 0). Better: Rely on payment processor validation.

issues.description: Card number stored in database (even last-4 digits). Storing any card data violates PCI DSS requirements. Full card number should never be transmitted to or stored by application.
issues.suggestion: Remove cardNumber storage entirely. Store only payment gateway transaction ID, amount, timestamp, status. Do not store any card data locally.

issues.description: Insufficient error handling in chargeCard. Generic catch block logs error without context. Catches all errors including programming errors, returning false silently for critical issues.
issues.suggestion: Implement proper error handling distinguishing between PaymentGatewayError and unexpected errors. Log with context: { amount, userId, timestamp }

issues.description: hasFeatureAccess function doesn't handle JSON.parse failures. If stored features JSON is corrupted, function throws unhandled error and crashes.
issues.suggestion: Add try-catch around JSON.parse: try { const features = JSON.parse(subscription.features); } catch (error) { logger.error('Invalid features JSON'); return false; }

issues.description: getUserSubscription has same JSON.parse vulnerability. Corrupted features JSON causes crash instead of graceful handling.
issues.suggestion: Wrap JSON.parse in try-catch with proper error logging and fallback behavior.

issues.description: Magic numbers and string literals scattered throughout: pricing (9.99, 49.99), tax rate (0.08), processing fee (0.029), subscription duration (1 year).
issues.suggestion: Create constants file or config object: SUBSCRIPTION_CONFIG = { premium: { price: 9.99 }, enterprise: { price: 49.99 }, taxRate: 0.08, processingFee: 0.029, durationYears: 1 }

issues.description: processPremiumPayment calculates price internally but payment object contains amount. No validation that these match, creating mismatch risk.
issues.suggestion: Validate amount matches calculated price. Better: Remove amount from client payment object and always calculate server-side.

issues.description: upgradeUserSubscription converts features array to JSON string with JSON.stringify on every payment. Features are static and shouldn't be serialized.
issues.suggestion: Store feature_tier enum/integer in subscriptions table that maps to static feature arrays. Query: 'INSERT INTO subscriptions (user_id, tier, valid_until)' then join with feature definitions.

issues.description: hasFeatureAccess and getUserSubscription query database on every call without caching. No connection pooling visible. Causes N+1 query problems.
issues.suggestion: Implement caching with Redis (5-minute TTL). Check cache first before querying: const cached = cache.get(userId); if (cached && !isExpired(cached)) return cached;

issues.description: Hardcoded SQL queries repeated with inconsistent parameter usage. No transactions. No rollback mechanism if payment succeeds but subscription update fails.
issues.suggestion: Wrap payment flow in database transaction: await db.transaction(async (trx) => { await chargeCard(...); await upgradeUserSubscription(...); })

issues.description: PaymentDetails interface lacks documentation of data flow and security concerns. No indication that this should be ephemeral.
issues.suggestion: Add JSDoc deprecation warning: /** @deprecated Use payment gateway tokens instead. Never store this data. Card details must be sent directly to PCI-compliant processor. */

issues.description: File starts with comments warning about no tests (⚠️ NO TESTS), but no test file exists and no enforcement mechanism.
issues.suggestion: Create src/premium.test.ts with comprehensive test suites. Require tests before merging via CI/CD rules.

issues.description: processPremiumPayment has no error recovery path. If upgradeUserSubscription fails after successful charge, user is charged but not upgraded.
issues.suggestion: Add error handling and logging: catch (error) { logger.error('Upgrade failed after charge', { userId }); throw new Error('Payment charged but subscription not updated - manual intervention needed'); }

issues.description: hasFeatureAccess checks 'if (rows.length === 0)' but should use more idiomatic null checks. TypeScript arrays should use optional chaining.
issues.suggestion: Use: const subscription = rows[0]; if (!subscription) { return false; }

issues.description: Subscription interface uses string[] for features, but features array is static and known. Should use discriminated union or enum.
issues.suggestion: Define: type FeatureType = 'unlimited_todos' | 'priority_support' | 'custom_themes' | 'api_access' | 'team_collaboration'; interface Subscription { features: FeatureType[]; }

issues.description: chargeCard function comment says 'Simulate payment gateway call' but actually tries to insert into database. Suggests incomplete implementation.
issues.suggestion: Either implement real payment gateway integration (Stripe/Square) or clearly mark as mock for testing. Update comment appropriately.

codeQuality.summary: CRITICAL FILE: This payment processing code has severe security vulnerabilities violating PCI DSS compliance. Core issues: (1) Handling raw credit card data instead of using tokenization, (2) Storing card info in database, (3) Weak card validation logic, (4) Missing transaction atomicity between payment and subscription, (5) No error handling for JSON deserialization. File requires complete architectural redesign to use PCI-compliant payment processor (Stripe/Square). Currently unsuitable for production. Additional issues: missing test coverage, no database query caching, absent transaction management.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Core payment processing function handling financial transactions. Untested payment flow could lead to data corruption, billing errors, and security vulnerabilities.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test successful premium subscription payment: verify payment is validated, correct amount is calculated, card is charged, and subscription is upgraded. Test both 'premium' and 'enterprise' tiers.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Security-critical validation preventing invalid payments. Failure to test allows malformed payment data to reach payment gateway.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test that processPremiumPayment throws 'Invalid payment details' error when validatePaymentDetails returns false. Mock validatePaymentDetails to return false.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Financial logic preventing underpayment. Without testing, users could pay less than required.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test that processPremiumPayment throws 'Insufficient payment amount' when payment.amount < calculated price. Test both tier types.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Error handling for failed card charges. Testing ensures failed payments don't create orphaned subscriptions.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test that processPremiumPayment returns false and does NOT upgrade subscription when chargeCard returns false. Verify upgradeUserSubscription is never called.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Payment validation is security-critical. Invalid card data could bypass gateway validation and cause failures.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test all validation rules: card 16 digits, CVV 3-4 digits, expiry MM/YY format with valid month, card not expired.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Boundary condition: 15/17-digit cards should fail, only 16 should pass.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test card numbers of lengths 15, 16, 17. Only 16 should return true.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Some cards have 3-digit CVV, others 4. Both should be accepted, 2 or 5 should fail.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test CVV lengths 2, 3, 4, 5. Only 3 and 4 should return true.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Regex must enforce MM/YY format. Invalid formats could cause crashes.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test invalid formats: '13/25' (invalid month), '1/25' (no leading zero), '12-25' (wrong separator). All should fail.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Card expiring current/next month should be handled correctly. Test ensures off-by-one errors don't occur.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test with current month (should be expired) and next month (should be valid).

untestedPaths.reasoning: Financial calculation. Incorrect pricing leads to revenue loss or customer overcharging.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Premium: 9.99 * 1.109 = 10.9772, Enterprise: 49.99 * 1.109 = 54.8773. Verify exact calculations.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Floating point arithmetic may produce unexpected rounding.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test that precise decimal values are returned and rounding matches payment gateway expectations.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Actual payment processing with database writes. Untested code could result in duplicate charges or orphaned records.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test that chargeCard calls db.query with correct parameters, extracts last 4 digits correctly, returns true on success. Mock db.query.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Error scenario handling for database/gateway failures. Without testing, unhandled exceptions can occur.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test that chargeCard returns false and logs error when db.query throws. Verify error doesn't propagate.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Security-sensitive: extracting last 4 digits must work correctly.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test that chargeCard correctly extracts last 4 digits from 16-digit card number.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Subscription data mutation. Untested database writes could result in inconsistent user data or failed upgrades.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test that upgradeUserSubscription calls db.query with correct parameters: userId, tier, validUntil (1 year), and correct features for each tier.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Different tiers have different features. Incorrect features could give unauthorized access.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test that premium gets ['unlimited_todos', 'priority_support', 'custom_themes'] and enterprise gets all plus ['api_access', 'team_collaboration'].

untestedPaths.reasoning: Date calculation for expiration. Off-by-one errors affect service availability.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test that validUntil is exactly 1 year from current date. Verify year incremented correctly.

untestedPaths.reasoning: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT behavior for new vs existing users is unverified.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test both INSERT (new user) and UPDATE (existing user) paths. Verify data correctly updated.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Feature access control is security-critical. Untested function could grant unauthorized access.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test that hasFeatureAccess returns true for valid subscription with feature, false when user doesn't exist.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Non-premium users should be denied access. Test ensures basic access control.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test that hasFeatureAccess returns false when no subscription exists (rows.length === 0).

untestedPaths.reasoning: Expired subscriptions should not grant access. Without testing, expired users retain premium access.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test that hasFeatureAccess returns false when valid_until is in the past, even if features array contains requested feature.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Users should only access purchased features. Without testing, unauthorized access is possible.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test that hasFeatureAccess returns false when requested feature is not in features array, even with valid subscription.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Expiring today should be expired, expiring tomorrow should be valid.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test with valid_until = today (expect false) and valid_until = tomorrow (expect true if feature exists).

untestedPaths.reasoning: Data retrieval and transformation. Untested JSON parsing could cause crashes or return corrupted data.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test that getUserSubscription returns correctly mapped Subscription with userId, tier, validUntil (Date), and features (parsed from JSON).

untestedPaths.reasoning: Should return null for non-existent subscriptions.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test that getUserSubscription returns null when no subscription exists (rows.length === 0).

untestedPaths.reasoning: Malformed features JSON causes crash. No try-catch present.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test that getUserSubscription handles invalid JSON gracefully (should add try-catch with error handling).

untestedPaths.reasoning: Database columns must correctly map to Subscription interface.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test that row.user_id -> userId, row.tier -> tier, row.valid_until -> Date, row.features -> parsed array.

testCoverage.summary: CRITICAL: Zero test coverage on critical payment processing module. All 6 exported/main functions and 4 helper functions completely untested. Major gaps: payment processing validation/error handling, card validation rules/edge cases, pricing calculations, database operations, feature access control, date/time boundaries. Additionally, syntax error on line 114 (missing quote after slice(-4)). Comprehensive tests required before production, prioritizing payment processing, card validation, feature access control, and subscription expiration logic.

refactorings.summary: Premium.ts requires significant refactoring across configuration management, code duplication, type safety, function complexity, and error handling. Priority refactorings: (1) Extract configuration constants (pricing, features, durations) to module level, (2) Create separate validation functions for all payment/subscription logic, (3) Add proper type definitions for database rows, (4) Break down complex orchestration functions into smaller units. These changes will improve testability (critical given test coverage warnings), maintainability, and readability.

recommendations.description: URGENT: Remove all raw credit card data handling. The PaymentDetails interface exposes cardNumber, expiryDate, and cvv which violate PCI DSS compliance. Implement tokenization using a PCI-compliant payment processor (Stripe, Square) immediately. Never handle, validate, or store card data in this application.

Remove card data storage from database. The chargeCard function stores card last-4 digits in the payments table, which still violates PCI compliance. Store only payment gateway transaction ID, amount, timestamp, and status.

Create comprehensive test suite for src/premium.ts. This module handles critical payment processing with zero test coverage. Prioritize testing: processPremiumPayment() flow, payment validation edge cases, feature access control, subscription expiration boundaries, and error scenarios.

Add transaction atomicity between payment processing and subscription upgrade. If chargeCard() succeeds but upgradeUserSubscription() fails, user is charged but not upgraded. Wrap both operations in a database transaction with rollback capability.

Add error handling for JSON.parse operations. Functions hasFeatureAccess() (line 150) and getUserSubscription() (line 173) will crash if features JSON is corrupted. Add try-catch blocks with graceful fallback behavior.

Extract configuration constants to module level. Magic numbers for pricing (9.99, 49.99), tax rate (0.08), processing fee (0.029), and subscription duration (1 year) are scattered throughout. Create SUBSCRIPTION_CONFIG constant object for maintainability and to prevent pricing errors.

Implement caching for subscription queries. hasFeatureAccess() and getUserSubscription() query the database on every call without caching. Add Redis-based caching with 5-minute TTL to reduce N+1 query problems and improve performance.

Fix weak expiry date validation logic. Current implementation creates date at start of expiry month instead of end, potentially allowing expired cards. Better: rely on payment processor validation instead of local validation.

Improve error handling and logging. Generic catch blocks with console.error lack context for debugging. Implement structured error logging with metadata (amount, userId, timestamp) and distinguish between PaymentGatewayError and unexpected errors.

Refactor feature management. Currently features are stored as serialized JSON strings on every subscription upgrade. Use feature_tier enum/integer instead, mapping to static feature arrays at query time. This improves performance and type safety.
